content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint lacks explicit estimand attributes for population and variable",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of proportion of patients achieving an IGA score of 0 or 1 on hand and foot at week 16 will be analyzed using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test",
      "page": 86,
      "section": "11.4.3.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary estimand table (Table 2) describes intercurrent event strategies and missing data handling, but the population (FAS) and variable (IGA score) are not explicitly stated as estimand attributes in the table or surrounding text, though they are mentioned elsewhere. The estimand framework requires clear specification of population, variable, intercurrent events, and summary measure.",
      "fix": "Explicitly state the population (FAS) and variable (IGA hand and foot score) in the estimand description or table."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "Proportion of patients with improvement (reduction) of weekly average of daily hand and foot peak Pruritus NRS ≥4 from baseline to week 16",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "This key secondary endpoint is listed but no statistical analysis method is described for it in the statistical plan. The plan only details the primary efficacy analysis; secondary endpoints are not addressed.",
      "fix": "Add analysis methods for all secondary endpoints, including the key secondary endpoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of multiplicity for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "Secondary Endpoint for Efficacy:",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol lists multiple secondary endpoints but does not describe any multiplicity control strategy (e.g., hierarchical testing, alpha adjustment) for these endpoints. This is a critical gap for confirmatory secondary inferences.",
      "fix": "Specify the multiplicity adjustment or hierarchical testing procedure for secondary endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "In patients with AD lesions on other parts of the body in addition to hands and feet; − Percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "4.1.4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Exploratory endpoints are listed but no statistical analysis methods are provided for them in the statistical plan.",
      "fix": "Add analysis methods for exploratory endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing data handling for secondary endpoints not specified",
      "quote": "Handling of missing data due to the COVID-19 pandemic and any additional analyses required to investigate the impact of COVID-19 to understand estimated treatment effect and safety will be detailed in the SAP.",
      "page": 84,
      "section": "11",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol only mentions missing data handling for the primary endpoint and defers COVID-19 related missing data to the SAP. It does not specify how missing data will be handled for secondary endpoints, which is a gap.",
      "fix": "Describe missing data handling strategies for secondary endpoints or state that they will be detailed in the SAP."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size section not provided",
      "quote": "The primary objective of the study is to assess the efficacy of dupilumab on skin lesions in patients with atopic hand and foot dermatitis.",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not include a sample size determination section. The extracted facts do not contain any sample size inputs, and the provided text does not mention sample size calculations. This is a critical omission for a protocol.",
      "fix": "Add a sample size section with assumptions (e.g., expected response rates, alpha, power) and justification."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of primary endpoint in hypothesis vs. endpoint section",
      "quote": "the success rate (where success is proportion of patients achieving an IGA score of 0 or 1 on hand and foot at week 16) is equal between dupilumab and placebo",
      "page": 84,
      "section": "11.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The hypothesis states 'IGA score of 0 or 1 on hand and foot' while the endpoint section says 'IGA (hand and foot) score of 0 or 1'. This is a minor wording inconsistency but could cause confusion.",
      "fix": "Use consistent terminology for the primary endpoint across sections."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety endpoint lacks analysis details",
      "quote": "Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) through week 16",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint is listed but no statistical analysis method is described for it. The safety analysis set is defined, but the analysis approach for TEAEs is not specified.",
      "fix": "Add a description of safety analyses, including how TEAEs will be summarized and compared."
    }
  ]
}
